Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study employs both bottom-up and top-down proteomics to characterize the ADP-ribosylation of EF-Tu. The bottom-up part uses a non-specific digestion (Nepenthes digestive fluid) and DDA acquisition. The top-down part uses HCD/EThcD on a specific charge state. The primary PTM of interest is ADP-ribosylation (+541.06 Da) on Aspartate 21.

scope: The purified EF-Tu toxin, after TreTu action or not, bound to GTP or GppNp, was buffer-exchanged with 200 mM NH4CH3COO using a BioSpin 6 (Bio-Rad).
The ADP-ribosylated EF-Tu protein bound to GTP was nanoelectrosprayed using a TriVersa NanoMate (Advion Biosciences) coupled to an Eclipse mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific).
About 100 μg of the different EF-Tu preparations were digested at 37°C for 10 min in acid condition (0.1% formic acid [FA]) by 1 μl of Nepenthes digestive fluid as described.
